chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Wahb ibn Abd Rabbih, who said:

I said to Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), 'Does a man perform Hajj on behalf of the Nasibi?' So he (peace be upon him) said, 'No.' I said, 'And if it was my father?' He (peace be upon him) said, 'So if it was your father, then yes.'
ai.seo_question: Can a man perform Hajj on behalf of a Nasibi or his own father?
ai.summary: In this concise narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) distinguishes between a general 'Nasibi' (adversary of the Ahl al-Bayt) and one's own father, permitting Hajj for the latter despite their potential sectarian opposition. This ruling highlights the Shia juristic principle that familial piety and respect (*birr al-walidayn*) can override sectarian enmity in the context of obligatory acts of worship, ensuring the spiritual benefit reaches the deceased relative.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Wahab Bin Abd Rabbih who said,

‘I said to Abu Abdullahasws, ‘Can the man perform Hajj on behalf of the Nasibi (Hostile one)?’ So heasws said: ‘No’. I said, ‘Supposing it was my father?’ Heasws said: ‘So if it was your father, then yes’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Wahab ibn ‘ Abd Rabbihi who has said the following:

“I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, if al-Hajj can be performed on behalf of one hostile to ’A’immah. He (the Imam) said, ‘No, it cannot be performed.’ I then asked, ‘Even if he is my father?’ He (the Imam) said, ‘If he is your father it is permissible.’”
